    rw [bit] at hit
    have truth : decide (p < n+b.length) = true := decide_eq_true inside
    change CompHalt C e mode f h B (some (.seek true), v, none)
      (if mode then decide (p < n+b.length) else b.getD (p-n) false)
    rw [truth]
    exact path.halt hit
  · have cond : ¬ v 5 < v 13 + b.length := by simpa [hq, hi, n] using inside
    simp only [if_neg cond, ↓reduceIte] at seek
    let vf := Function.update (Function.update v 0 (v 3)) 13 (v 13+b.length)
    have bf : ∀ r, vf r ≤ B := register_update_le _ 13 B _
      (register_update_le v 0 B _ hv (hv 3)) (by simpa [hi] using total)
    have bit : b.getD (p-n) false = false := by
      simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega : b.length ≤ p-n)]
    have ans : (if mode then decide (p < n+b.length) else b.getD (p-n) false) = false := by
      simp only [inside, decide_false, bit, ite_self]
    rw [ans]
    exact seek.halt (comp_ret C e mode false f h B vf bf)

/-- Both separator cells and the following suffix have the exact paired-output semantics.

**Proof sketch.** Test the current output position, then the following position, returning
`false,true` for bit queries and accepting both for length queries. If neither matches,
advance past the separator and seek the retained suffix at its saved physical start. -/
private lemma comp_separator_run (C e : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool)
    (x b : List Bool) (p B : ℕ) (v : Fin 14 → ℕ) (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B)
    (he : v 3 = 2*(pairEncode x b).length) (hb : v 4 = 4*x.length+4)
    (hi : v 13 = 2*(f x).length) (hq : v 5 = p) (le : 2*(f x).length ≤ p)
    (total : (pairEncode (f x) b).length ≤ B) :
    CompHalt C e mode f (pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)) B (some (.separator false), v, none)
      (if mode then decide (p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length) else (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false) := by
  let h := pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)
  let n := 2*(f x).length
  have outlen : (pairEncode (f x) b).length = n+2+b.length := length_pairEncode _ _
  have firsteq : (if mode then decide (n < (pairEncode (f x) b).length)
      else (pairEncode (f x) b).getD n false) = mode := by
    have lt : n < (pairEncode (f x) b).length := by omega
    cases mode with
    | false =>
      change (pairEncode (f x) b).getD n false = false
      rw [pairEncode_getD, if_neg (by dsimp [n]; omega), if_pos rfl]
    | true => simp [lt]
  by_cases first : p = n
  · have eq : v 13 = v 5 := by omega
    have ans : (if mode then decide (p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length)
        else (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false) = mode := by simpa only [first] using firsteq
    rw [ans]
    apply AHalt.step ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, hv⟩
    simpa only [astep_jeq (show compARM C e mode (.separator false) = _ from rfl), if_pos eq] using
      comp_ret C e mode mode f h B v hv
  · have ne : v 13 ≠ v 5 := by omega
    let v₁ := Function.update v 13 (n+1)
    have b₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := register_update_le v 13 B _ hv (by omega)
    have headRun : CompReach C e mode f h B (some (.separator false), v, none)
        (some (.separator true), v₁, none) := by
      apply AReach.step ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, hv⟩
      simp only [astep_jeq (show compARM C e mode (.separator false) = _ from rfl), if_neg ne]
      simpa only [astep_inc (show compARM C e mode (.separatorInc false) = _ from rfl), hi] using
        (AReach.single (A := compARM C e mode) (oracle := compOracle f) (x := h)
          (a := (some (.separatorInc false), v, none)) ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, hv⟩)
    by_cases second : p = n+1
    · have eq : v₁ 13 = v₁ 5 := by simp [v₁, hq, second]
      have ans : (if mode then decide (p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length)
          else (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false) = true := by
        have lt : p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length := by omega
        cases mode with
        | false =>
          change (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false = true
          rw [pairEncode_getD, if_neg (by dsimp [n] at second; omega),
            if_neg (by dsimp [n] at second; omega), if_pos (by dsimp [n] at second; omega)]
        | true => simp [lt]
      rw [ans]
      apply headRun.halt
      apply AHalt.step ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, b₁⟩
      simpa only [astep_jeq (show compARM C e mode (.separator true) = _ from rfl), if_pos eq] using
        comp_ret C e mode true f h B v₁ b₁
    · have beyond : n+2 ≤ p := by omega
      have ne₁ : v₁ 13 ≠ v₁ 5 := by simp [v₁, hq]; omega
      let v₂ := Function.update v 13 (n+2)
      let vz := Function.update v₂ 0 0
      let vs := Function.update v₂ 0 (v 4)
      have b₂ : ∀ r, v₂ r ≤ B := register_update_le v 13 B _ hv (by omega)
      have bz : ∀ r, vz r ≤ B := register_update_le v₂ 0 B 0 b₂ (Nat.zero_le _)
      have bs : ∀ r, vs r ≤ B := register_update_le v₂ 0 B _ b₂ (hv 4)
      have copy : CompReach C e mode f h B (some (.copy 7 false), vz, none) (some (.seek true), vs, none) := by
        simpa [vz, vs, v₂, compCopy] using comp_copy_run C e mode f h B 7 vz bz (by simp [vz, compCopy])
      have move : CompReach C e mode f h B (some (.separator true), v₁, none) (some (.seek true), vs, none) := by
        apply AReach.step ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, b₁⟩
        simp only [astep_jeq (show compARM C e mode (.separator true) = _ from rfl), if_neg ne₁]
        apply AReach.step ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, b₁⟩
        simp only [astep_inc (show compARM C e mode (.separatorInc true) = _ from rfl), v₁,
          Function.update_self, Function.update_idem]
        change CompReach C e mode f h B (some .suffixReset, v₂, none) _
        apply AReach.step ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, b₂⟩
        exact copy
      have suffix := comp_suffix_run C e mode f x b p B vs bs (by simp [vs, hb])
        (by simp [vs, v₂, he]) (by simp [vs, v₂, n]) (by simp [vs, v₂, hq]) beyond
        (by simpa [outlen, n] using total)
      have bit : (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false = b.getD (p-(n+2)) false := by
        rw [pairEncode_getD, if_neg (by dsimp [n] at beyond; omega),
          if_neg (by dsimp [n] at beyond; omega), if_neg (by dsimp [n] at beyond; omega)]
        congr 1
      simpa only [outlen, bit] using (headRun.trans move).halt suffix

/-- Lookup first seeks within the doubled virtual output of `f`, then delegates the two
separator cells and the retained suffix to their common continuation.

**Proof sketch.** The prefix seek is virtual stride one, so a hit is answered by the
lifted bit at half its index. A miss has index exactly twice the output length. This
includes an empty `f` output and flows into the proved separator/suffix continuation. -/
private lemma comp_lookup_run (C e : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool)
    (x b : List Bool) (p B : ℕ) (v : Fin 14 → ℕ) (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B)
    (hp : v 0 = 0) (he : v 3 = 2*(pairEncode x b).length) (hb : v 4 = 4*x.length+4)
    (hf : v 11 = 2*(f x).length) (hi : v 13 = 0) (hq : v 5 = p)
    (total : (pairEncode (f x) b).length ≤ B) :
    CompHalt C e mode f (pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)) B (some (.seek false), v, none)
      (if mode then decide (p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length) else (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false) := by
  let h := pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)
  let n := 2*(f x).length
  have nb : n ≤ B := by rw [length_pairEncode] at total; omega
  have seek := comp_seek_run C e mode false f h B n v hv
    (by simpa [hp, compStride, n] using hf) (by simpa [hi] using nb) (by simp [hi])
  by_cases inside : p < n
  · have cond : v 5 < v 13+n := by omega
    simp only [if_pos cond, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte] at seek
    let vh := Function.update (Function.update v 0 p) 13 p
    have bh : ∀ r, vh r ≤ B := register_update_le _ 13 B p
      (register_update_le v 0 B p hv (by omega)) (by omega)
    have path : CompReach C e mode f h B (some (.seek false), v, none) (some .prefixHit, vh, none) := by
      simpa [vh, hp, hi, hq, compStride] using seek
    have ans : (if mode then true else (f x).getD (vh 0/2) false) =
        (if mode then decide (p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length) else (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false) := by
      have lt : p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length := by rw [length_pairEncode]; dsimp [n] at inside; omega
      cases mode with
      | false =>
        change (f x).getD (p/2) false = (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false
        rw [pairEncode_getD, if_pos inside]
      | true => simp [lt]
    rw [← ans]
    exact path.halt (comp_prefix_hit C e mode f x b p B vh bh)
  · have cond : ¬ v 5 < v 13+n := by omega
    simp only [if_neg cond, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte] at seek
    let vm := Function.update (Function.update v 0 (v 11)) 13 n
    have bm : ∀ r, vm r ≤ B := register_update_le _ 13 B n (register_update_le v 0 B _ hv (hv 11)) nb
    have path : CompReach C e mode f h B (some (.seek false), v, none) (some (.separator false), vm, none) := by
      simpa [vm, hi] using seek
    exact path.halt (comp_separator_run C e mode f x b p B vm bm (by simp [vm, he])
      (by simp [vm, hb]) (by simp [vm, n]) (by simp [vm, hq]) (by omega) total)


/-- The canonicality predicate exactly matches the frozen reshaping definition. -/
private lemma compQ_field (f : List Bool → List Bool) (x b : List Bool) :
    compQ f (pairEncode x b) = if Canon b then pairEncode (f x) b else [] := by
  have canon : (Nat.bits (bitsVal b) = b) ↔ Canon b :=
    ⟨fun eq => eq ▸ canon_bits _, fun hc => (canon_eq_bits b hc).symm⟩
  simp only [compQ, pairDecode_pairEncode, canon]

/-- The two query languages share the program's mode bit. -/
private def compLang (f : List Bool → List Bool) (mode : Bool) : Language Bool :=
  indexLang fun z p => if mode then p < (compQ f z).length else (compQ f z).getD p false = true

/-- On a genuine outer query, the indicator is exactly the requested output bit or boundary test. -/
private lemma comp_lang_pair (f : List Bool → List Bool) (mode : Bool) (z : List Bool) (p : ℕ) :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (compLang f mode : Set (List Bool)) (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)) =
      if mode then decide (p < (compQ f z).length) else (compQ f z).getD p false := by
  rw [compLang, indicator_indexLang_pairEncode]
  cases mode <;> simp

/-- A word with no canonical paired representation is rejected in either mode. -/
private lemma comp_bad_query (f : List Bool → List Bool) (mode : Bool) (h : List Bool)
    (bad : ∀ z p, h ≠ pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)) :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (compLang f mode : Set (List Bool)) h = false := by
  apply Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr
  intro accepts
  rw [indicator_eq_decide, decide_eq_true_eq] at accepts
  obtain ⟨z, p, eq, _⟩ := accepts
  exact bad z p eq

/-- Both outer-tail failure modes have false answers. Width rejection uses the full
composition bound; no unbounded numerical query is stored. -/
private lemma comp_rejected_tail {f : List Bool → List Bool} {C e : ℕ}
    (hf : ∀ x, (f x).length ≤ C * (x.length+1)^e) (mode : Bool) (z tail : List Bool)
    (bad : ¬ (Canon tail ∧ tail.length ≤ (Nat.bits ((2*C+3)*((pairEncode z tail).length+1)^(e+1))).length)) :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (compLang f mode : Set (List Bool)) (pairEncode z tail) = false := by
  by_cases canonical : Canon tail
  · obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ : ∃ p, tail = Nat.bits p := ⟨bitsVal tail, canon_eq_bits tail canonical⟩
    have wide : (Nat.bits ((2*C+3)*((pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length+1)^(e+1))).length <
        (Nat.bits p).length := Nat.lt_of_not_ge (fun width => bad ⟨canon_bits p, width⟩)
    have overflow := compQ_query_overflow hf z p wide
    rw [comp_lang_pair]
    cases mode with
    | false => exact overflow.1
    | true => simp only [↓reduceIte, overflow.2, decide_false]
  · apply comp_bad_query
    intro w p eq
    have fields := pairEncode_injective (a₁ := (z, tail)) (a₂ := (w, Nat.bits p)) eq
    have word : tail = Nat.bits p := congrArg Prod.snd fields
    exact canonical (word.symm ▸ canon_bits p)

/-- After valid inner syntax, compute the capped length and perform the output lookup.

**Proof sketch.** Compute the exact polynomial cap at `|x|+1`; the capped truthful search
returns `|f x|`, including equality with the cap and cap zero. The public fixed transfer
doubles this length into the virtual prefix boundary. Clear the pointer and use the
proved output-layout run. The full composition bound covers every output counter. -/
private lemma comp_valid_inner (C e : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool)
    (bound : ∀ x, (f x).length ≤ C*(x.length+1)^e) (x b : List Bool) (p : ℕ)
    (canonical : Canon b) (v : Fin 14 → ℕ)
    (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ compBound C e (pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)).length)
    (he : v 3 = 2*(pairEncode x b).length) (hb : v 4 = 4*x.length+4) (hq : v 5 = p)
    (ht : v 6 = 0) (ha : v 7 = 0) (hi : v 10 = 0) (hs : v 11 = 0)
    (hf : v 12 = 0) (hj : v 13 = 0) :
    CompHalt C e mode f (pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p))
      (compBound C e (pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)).length)
      (some .innerPrepare, v, none)
      (if mode then decide (p < (pairEncode (f x) b).length) else (pairEncode (f x) b).getD p false) := by
  let h := pairEncode (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)
  let B := compBound C e h.length
  have xn : x.length ≤ h.length := by simp only [h, length_pairEncode]; omega
  have room := comp_bound_room C e h.length
  have output : (pairEncode (f x) b).length ≤ B := by
    have cap := compQ_host_cap bound (pairEncode x b) (Nat.bits p)
    rw [compQ_field, if_pos canonical] at cap
    change (pairEncode (f x) b).length ≤ (2*C+3)*(h.length+1)^(e+1) at cap
    dsimp [B]
    omega
  have dbl : 2*(f x).length ≤ B := by rw [length_pairEncode] at output; omega
  let vp := Function.update (Function.update v 8 (x.length+1)) 7 (C*(x.length+1)^e)
  let vs := Function.update vp 12 (f x).length
  let vd := Function.update (Function.update vs 12 0) 11 (2*(f x).length)
  let vl := Function.update vd 0 0
  have powers := comp_power_bound C e h.length (x.length+1) e false (by omega) (by omega)
  have bp : ∀ r, vp r ≤ B := register_update_le _ 7 B _
    (register_update_le v 8 B _ hv (by omega)) (by simpa [compFactor] using powers.2)
  have bs : ∀ r, vs r ≤ B := register_update_le vp 12 B _ bp (by omega)
  have bd : ∀ r, vd r ≤ B := register_update_le _ 11 B _
    (register_update_le vs 12 B 0 bs (Nat.zero_le _)) dbl
  have bl : ∀ r, vl r ≤ B := register_update_le vd 0 B 0 bd (Nat.zero_le _)
  have polynomial := comp_inner_prepare C e mode f h x.length v hv hb ht ha hi hs xn
  have search := comp_length_search C e mode f h B (f x).length vp bp
    (by simp [vp, hf]) (by simpa [vp] using bound x)
    (by intro i _; simpa [h] using comp_lifted f true x b p i)
  have double : CompReach C e mode f h B (some .doubleTest, vs, none) (some .lookupReset, vd, none) := by
    have move := registerScale_loop (compARM C e mode) (compOracle f) h 12 11 (by decide)
      .doubleTest .doubleDown .lookupReset
      (fun i => if i = 0 then .doubleInc false else if i = 1 then .doubleInc true else .doubleTest)
      2 rfl rfl
      (by
        intro i hi
        have cases : i = 0 ∨ i = 1 := by omega
        rcases cases with rfl | rfl <;> rfl)
      rfl B vs bs (by simpa [vs, vp, hs] using dbl)
    simpa [vd, vs, vp, hs] using move
  have lookup := comp_lookup_run C e mode f x b p B vl bl (by simp [vl])
    (by simp [vl, vd, vs, vp, he]) (by simp [vl, vd, vs, vp, hb])
    (by simp [vl, vd]) (by simp [vl, vd, vs, vp, hj]) (by simp [vl, vd, vs, vp, hq]) output
  apply (polynomial.trans (search.trans double)).halt
  apply AHalt.step ⟨comp_preS C e mode h _, bd⟩
  exact lookup

/-- Inner shape and canonicality validation lead either to false or to the proved valid
inner computation. Arbitrary first fields and arbitrarily large canonical suffixes are
allowed.

**Proof sketch.** The received stride-two pair scan locates the inner suffix. A malformed
pair gives the empty reshaping. Save the suffix boundary and invoke the independent
last-bit canonicality check; its failure also gives the empty reshaping. Otherwise all
scratch is still clear, so the valid-inner computation applies. -/
private lemma comp_inner_run (C e : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool)
    (bound : ∀ x, (f x).length ≤ C*(x.length+1)^e) (z : List Bool) (p : ℕ)
    (pb : p ≤ compBound C e (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length) :
    CompHalt C e mode f (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)) (compBound C e (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length)
      (some (.scan true), compValues (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length
        (tail := 2*z.length+2) (stop := 2*z.length) (query := p)
        (base := (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length+1), none)
      (if mode then decide (p < (compQ f z).length) else (compQ f z).getD p false) := by
  let h := pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)
  let B := compBound C e h.length
  let v := compValues h.length (tail := 2*z.length+2) (stop := 2*z.length) (query := p) (base := h.length+1)
  change p ≤ B at pb
  have room := (comp_bound_room C e h.length).1
  have len : h.length = 2*z.length+2+(Nat.bits p).length := length_pairEncode _ _
  have bv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B := by simp [v, compValues, Fin.forall_fin_succ]; dsimp [B] at *; omega
  have scan := comp_pair_run C e mode true f h z B v bv (by simp [v, compLimit, compStride])
    (by intro i hi; simpa [v, compStride] using drop_first_read z (Nat.bits p) i hi)
  cases shape : pairDecode z with
  | none =>
    simp only [shape] at scan
    obtain ⟨t, tl, path⟩ := scan
    have bp : v 0 + compStride true*t ≤ B := by simp [v, compStride]; dsimp [B] at *; omega
    have out : compQ f z = [] := by simp [compQ, shape]
    simp only [out, List.length_nil, Nat.not_lt_zero, decide_false, List.getD_nil, ite_self]
    exact path.halt (comp_ret C e mode false f h B _ (register_update_le v 0 B _ bv bp))
  | some pair =>
    rcases pair with ⟨x, b⟩
    have eq := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z x b shape
    subst z
    simp only [pairDecode_pairEncode] at scan
    let va := Function.update v 0 (4*x.length+4)
    let vb := Function.update va 4 (4*x.length+4)
    have addr : 4*x.length+4 ≤ B := by
      have vl : 2*(pairEncode x b).length ≤ B := by simpa [v] using bv 3
      rw [length_pairEncode] at vl
      omega
    have ba : ∀ r, va r ≤ B := register_update_le v 0 B _ bv addr
    have bb : ∀ r, vb r ≤ B := register_update_le va 4 B _ ba addr
    have scanned : CompReach C e mode f h B (some (.scan true), v, none) (some (.copy 4 false), va, none) := by
      simpa [va, v, compStride, Nat.mul_add, ← Nat.mul_assoc] using scan
    have save : CompReach C e mode f h B (some (.copy 4 false), va, none) (some .canonical, vb, none) := by
      simpa [vb, va, compCopy] using comp_copy_run C e mode f h B 4 va ba (by simp [va, v, compCopy])
    obtain ⟨vc, bc, frame, canonical⟩ := comp_canonical_run C e mode f x b (Nat.bits p) B vb bb
      (by simp [vb, va, v]) (by simp [vb])
    by_cases canon : Canon b
    · simp only [if_pos canon] at canonical
      rw [compQ_field, if_pos canon]
      apply (scanned.trans (save.trans canonical)).halt
      apply comp_valid_inner C e mode f bound x b p canon vc bc
      all_goals first
        | (rw [frame _ (by decide)]; simp [vb, va, v])
    · simp only [if_neg canon] at canonical
      rw [compQ_field, if_neg canon]
      simp only [List.length_nil, Nat.not_lt_zero, decide_false, List.getD_nil, ite_self]
      exact (scanned.trans (save.trans canonical)).halt (comp_ret C e mode false f h B vc bc)


/-- The composition-query ARM halts correctly on every physical input within one fixed
polynomial register bound.

**Proof sketch.** Count the host and validate its outer pair. Save the pair boundaries,
construct the full output cap, and validate the canonical outer index before decoding.
Malformed or over-width queries reject by the proved language laws. The bounded decoded
query then enters the complete inner validation, capped search, and output-layout run. -/
private lemma comp_run (C e : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool)
    (bound : ∀ x, (f x).length ≤ C*(x.length+1)^e) (h : List Bool) :
    CompHalt C e mode f h (compBound C e h.length) (some .count, fun _ => 0, none)
      (MultiTapeTM.indicator (compLang f mode : Set (List Bool)) h) := by
  have room := (comp_bound_room C e h.length).1
  have count := inputLength_loop (compARM C e mode) (compOracle f) h 1 1 .count .countInc (.scan false)
    rfl rfl (fun i _ => comp_len f h i) (compBound C e h.length) (by omega) (fun _ => 0)
    (by intro r; exact Nat.zero_le _) (Nat.zero_le _)
  have vec : Function.update (fun _ : Fin 14 => 0) 1 h.length = compValues h.length := by
    have zero : (fun _ : Fin 14 => 0) = compValues 0 := by
      simp only [compValues, Matrix.vec_single_eq_const, Matrix.vecCons_const]
    rw [zero]
    simp
  rw [vec] at count
  have bv : ∀ r, (compValues h.length) r ≤ compBound C e h.length := by
    simp [compValues, Fin.forall_fin_succ]; omega
  have scan := comp_pair_run C e mode false f h h (compBound C e h.length) (compValues h.length) bv
    (by simp [compLimit, compStride]) (by intro i _; simp [compStride])
  cases shape : pairDecode h with
  | none =>
    simp only [shape] at scan
    obtain ⟨t, ht, path⟩ := scan
    have bp : (compValues h.length) 0 + compStride false*t ≤ compBound C e h.length := by
      simp [compStride]; omega
    have answer := comp_bad_query f mode h (by
      intro z p eq
      rw [eq, pairDecode_pairEncode] at shape
      contradiction)
    rw [answer]
    exact (count.trans path).halt (comp_ret C e mode false f h (compBound C e h.length) _
      (register_update_le (compValues h.length) 0 _ _ bv bp))
  | some pair =>
    rcases pair with ⟨z, tail⟩
    have eq := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode h z tail shape
    subst h
    simp only [pairDecode_pairEncode] at scan
    have start : CompReach C e mode f (pairEncode z tail) (compBound C e (pairEncode z tail).length)
        (some .count, fun _ => 0, none)
        (some (.copy 0 false), compValues (pairEncode z tail).length (ptr := 2*z.length+2), none) := by
      apply count.trans
      simpa [compStride] using scan
    have prepare := comp_outer_prepare C e mode f z tail
    have decode := comp_outer_decode C e mode f z tail
    dsimp only at prepare decode
    by_cases good : Canon tail ∧ tail.length ≤
        (Nat.bits ((2*C+3)*((pairEncode z tail).length+1)^(e+1))).length
    · simp only [if_pos good] at decode
      obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ : ∃ p, tail = Nat.bits p := ⟨bitsVal tail, canon_eq_bits tail good.1⟩
      have pb := query_index_bound p ((2*C+3)*((pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length+1)^(e+1)) good.2
      have bounded : p ≤ compBound C e (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length :=
        pb.trans (comp_bound_room C e (pairEncode z (Nat.bits p)).length).2
      simp only [bitsVal_bits] at decode
      rw [comp_lang_pair]
      exact (start.trans (prepare.trans decode)).halt (comp_inner_run C e mode f bound z p bounded)
    · simp only [if_neg good] at decode
      rw [comp_rejected_tail bound mode z tail good]
      exact (start.trans prepare).halt decode

/-- Compile the single mode-parametrized construction against the four proved languages. -/
private lemma comp_mem {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable f)
    (C e : ℕ) (bound : ∀ x, (f x).length ≤ C*(x.length+1)^e) (mode : Bool) :
    compLang f mode ∈ LOGSPACE := by
  apply arm_decides_poly (compARM C e mode) .count (compBank f) (compBank_mem hf)
    (8*(2*C+3)) (e+1)
  intro h
  exact comp_run C e mode f bound h

/-- **`comp`'s query reshaping is implicitly logspace computable** (phase P4.4b; proved): if `f` is, so is `compQ f`.

**Proof sketch.**

* **Bound.** `Complexity.compQ_length_le`.
* **The ARM.** Both query languages come from one abstract register machine with a mode bit
  over a four-oracle bank (`LogProg.arm_decides_poly`):
  * `inputBitLang` and `inputLenLang`;
  * `{z | dropIdx (dropIdx z) ∈ L}` for `L` each of `f`'s two query languages. These are in
    `L` by `Complexity.mem_LOGSPACE_preimage` twice along
    `Complexity.implicitlyLogspaceComputable_dropIdx`.

  A `whole` call on `[j]` from the host `h = ⟨w, bits p⟩` presents
  `⟨⟨w, bits p⟩, bits j⟩`, which two `dropIdx` turn into `⟨x, bits j⟩` (`dropIdx_pairEncode`).
* **The run** ([AB09, Lemma 4.17's proof]; the P4.4 audit's question-2 ledger):
  * (i) Validate `h`, with the overflow test before storing `p`.
  * (ii) Validate `w = ⟨x, b⟩` with `b` canonical: empty (the representation of `0`) or
    ending in `true`, using `LogProg.canon_eq_bits` and `LogProg.canon_bits`.
  * (iii) Find `F := |f x|` by lifted length queries at `j = 0, 1, …` while `j` is below the
    cap `C (|x| + 1)^e`. `F` is the first `j` whose query fails, or the cap itself when every
    query below it succeeds, since `|f x|` is at most the cap. A cap of `0` gives `F = 0`
    with no query.
  * (iv) Answer:
    * `p < 2F`: the lifted bit at `⌊p/2⌋`;
    * `p ∈ {2F, 2F + 1}`: the separator `[false, true]`;
    * otherwise: `b`'s bit at `p − 2F − 2`, read from `h` at its doubled position;
    * length: `p < 2F + 2 + |b|`. -/
theorem ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.compQ {f : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hf : ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable f) : ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable (compQ f) := by
  obtain ⟨C, e, bound⟩ := hf.1
  refine ⟨⟨2*C+3, e+1, compQ_length_le bound⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simpa only [compLang, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte] using comp_mem hf C e bound false
  · simpa only [compLang, ↓reduceIte] using comp_mem hf C e bound true

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Logspace/Reductions.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SpaceClasses
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ImplicitPoly
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Reductions
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.QueryReshape

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Logspace reductions and `NL`-completeness

[AB09, §4.3, Definition 4.16 and Lemma 4.17]: reductions computed in
logarithmic space — rendered, as the book does, through *implicitly* logspace
computable functions (`Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable`, the received
P0 surface), since a logspace machine cannot store its output. Phase P4.4 of
`AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`; the composition theorem stated here is
exactly the general Lemma 4.17 that the P0 reception round recorded as *not*
delivered (its note 10) — the received `UnaryLogspace.counterProg` closure
remains the special case.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogspaceReducible` (`≤ₗ`) — [AB09, Definition 4.16].
* `Complexity.NLComplete` — `NL`-membership plus `NL`-hardness under `≤ₗ`.
  [AB09, Definition 4.16]

## Main results (phase-P4.4 statements proved)

* `Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.comp` — the composition engine
  ([AB09, Lemma 4.17's proof], Figure 4.3's virtual input tape).
* `Complexity.LogspaceReducible.trans` — [AB09, Lemma 4.17(1)].
* `Complexity.mem_LOGSPACE_of_logspaceReducible` — [AB09, Lemma 4.17(2)].
* `Complexity.LogspaceReducible.polyTimeReducible` — `≤ₗ` refines `≤ₚ`.
* `Complexity.NL_eq_LOGSPACE_of_nlComplete_mem_LOGSPACE` — an `NL`-complete
  language in `L` collapses `NL` to `L`. [AB09, after Lemma 4.17]

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.3, Definition 4.16, Lemma 4.17,
  Figure 4.3.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- **Logspace reducibility** [AB09, Definition 4.16]: `B ≤ₗ C` when some
implicitly logspace computable `f` satisfies `x ∈ B ↔ f x ∈ C` for every
string — the reduction is never written down whole, only queried bit by bit
(`Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable`, with its received divergences:
`0`-based indices and the campaign polynomial normal form). -/
def LogspaceReducible (B C : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : List Bool → List Bool, ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable f ∧
    ∀ x, x ∈ B ↔ f x ∈ C

@[inherit_doc] scoped infix:50 " ≤ₗ " => LogspaceReducible

/-- **`NL`-completeness** [AB09, Definition 4.16]: membership in `NL`
together with `NL`-hardness under logspace reductions. (Polynomial-time
reductions would trivialize this notion — `Complexity.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_NL`,
Exercise 4.3, phase P4.2.) -/
def NLComplete (C : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  C ∈ NL ∧ ∀ B ∈ NL, B ≤ₗ C

/-- The composite output bound of [AB09, Lemma 4.17] (P4.4 audit, question 2).

**Proof sketch.** Absorb the added one into `C + 1`, apply the second polynomial
bound monotonically, and distribute powers. This is the pre-ship D2 bound. -/
private theorem comp_length_le {f g : List Bool → List Bool} {C c D d : ℕ}
    (hf : ∀ x, (f x).length ≤ C * (x.length + 1) ^ c)
    (hg : ∀ y, (g y).length ≤ D * (y.length + 1) ^ d) (x : List Bool) :
    (g (f x)).length ≤ D * (C + 1) ^ d * (x.length + 1) ^ (c * d) := by
  have h1 : 1 ≤ (x.length + 1) ^ c := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
  have h2 : (f x).length + 1 ≤ (C + 1) * (x.length + 1) ^ c := by
    have := hf x
    have e : (C + 1) * (x.length + 1) ^ c = C * (x.length + 1) ^ c + (x.length + 1) ^ c := by
      ring
    omega
  calc (g (f x)).length ≤ D * ((f x).length + 1) ^ d := hg _
    _ ≤ D * ((C + 1) * (x.length + 1) ^ c) ^ d :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left h2 d)
    _ = D * (C + 1) ^ d * (x.length + 1) ^ (c * d) := by rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul]; ring

/-- **Composition of implicitly logspace computable functions** ([AB09,
Lemma 4.17's proof]; proved — phase P4.4, **the general
composition the P0 round recorded as undelivered**): if `f` and `g` are
implicitly logspace computable, so is `g ∘ f`.

**Proof sketch.** [AB09, Figure 4.3]: to answer a bit or length query about
`g (f x)`, run `g`'s query machine against a **virtual input tape** holding
`f x` — maintain the index of the cell `g`'s head would scan (logarithmic in
`|f x|`, hence in `|x|` by `f`'s polynomial output bound), and whenever
`g`'s machine reads, suspend it and answer with `f`'s bit/length queries on
`⟨x, i⟩`. The received `LogProg` call protocol does not host this shape by
itself: a call's virtual input is read physically (the whole input, or its
leading run of `1`s, followed by register words), so no call can serve `g`'s
input from `f`'s queries (P0 reception audit, note 10). Fill route (phase
P4.4b, `audits/ch4-p44-resolutions-addendum.md`): both query languages of
`g ∘ f` are preimages of `g`'s along `Complexity.compQ f`
(`Complexity.mem_indexLang_compQ_iff`), hence in `L` by
`Complexity.mem_LOGSPACE_preimage` (the Fig. 4.3 engine,
`Complexity.LogProg.OIS`) and `Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.compQ`.
Obligations, named: the polynomial bound of the composite (`f`'s and `g`'s
bounds composed, `D (C + 1)^d (|x| + 1)^{cd}`); the two preimage memberships;
the index bookkeeping, which lives in `compQ`'s machines. (Sketch prose
corrected at phase P4.4b; the statement is unchanged.) -/
theorem ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.comp {f g : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hf : ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable f) (hg : ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable g) :
    ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable (g ∘ f) := by
  have hQ := hf.compQ
  obtain ⟨⟨C, c, hC⟩, -, -⟩ := hf
  obtain ⟨⟨D, d, hD⟩, hgb, hgl⟩ := hg
  refine ⟨⟨D * (C + 1) ^ d, c * d, comp_length_le (f := f) (g := g) hC hD⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [show indexLang (fun x i => ((g ∘ f) x).getD i false = true) =
        ({w | Complexity.compQ f w ∈ indexLang fun y i => (g y).getD i false = true} : Language Bool) from
      Set.ext (mem_indexLang_compQ_iff f fun y i => (g y).getD i false = true)]
    exact mem_LOGSPACE_preimage hQ hgb
  · rw [show indexLang (fun x i => i < ((g ∘ f) x).length) =
        ({w | Complexity.compQ f w ∈ indexLang fun y i => i < (g y).length} : Language Bool) from
      Set.ext (mem_indexLang_compQ_iff f fun y i => i < (g y).length)]
    exact mem_LOGSPACE_preimage hQ hgl

/-- **Logspace reducibility is transitive** ([AB09, Lemma 4.17(1)]; proved).

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.comp` on the two
reduction functions; the membership equivalences chain. -/
theorem LogspaceReducible.trans {B C D : Language Bool} (h₁ : B ≤ₗ C)
    (h₂ : C ≤ₗ D) : B ≤ₗ D := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hB⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨g, hg, hC⟩ := h₂
  exact ⟨g ∘ f, hf.comp hg, fun x => (hB x).trans (hC (f x))⟩

/-- **Logspace reductions preserve `L` downward** ([AB09, Lemma 4.17(2)];
proved): if `B ≤ₗ C` and `C ∈ LOGSPACE` then `B ∈ LOGSPACE`.

**Proof sketch.** Directly by the preimage theorem (route change 1 of
`audits/ch4-p44-resolutions-addendum.md`). Unpack `h` as an implicitly
logspace computable `f` with `x ∈ B ↔ f x ∈ C`. Then `B = {x | f x ∈ C}` by
`Set.ext`, and `Complexity.mem_LOGSPACE_preimage hf hC` concludes. The
preimage engine, the oracle-input simulator `Complexity.LogProg.OIS` ([AB09,
Fig. 4.3]'s construction), cites nothing from this file, so there is no
circularity (round-1 audit, finding 2). The earlier route through `C`'s
characteristic function and `comp` is superseded: deciding `χ_C`'s bit
language needs the engine itself. (Sketch prose corrected at the P4.4b
statement gate; the statement is unchanged.) -/
theorem mem_LOGSPACE_of_logspaceReducible {B C : Language Bool} (h : B ≤ₗ C)
    (hC : C ∈ LOGSPACE) : B ∈ LOGSPACE := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hB⟩ := h
  rw [show B = ({x | f x ∈ C} : Language Bool) from Set.ext hB]
  exact mem_LOGSPACE_preimage hf hC

/-- **`≤ₗ` refines `≤ₚ`**: a logspace reduction is in
particular a polynomial-time reduction.

**Proof sketch.** The received
`Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable.polyTimeComputable` turns the
implicit witness into a whole-output polynomial-time machine; the
equivalences carry over verbatim. -/
theorem LogspaceReducible.polyTimeReducible {B C : Language Bool}
    (h : B ≤ₗ C) : B ≤ₚ C := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hB⟩ := h
  exact ⟨f, hf.polyTimeComputable, hB⟩

/-- **An `NL`-complete language in `L` collapses `NL`** ([AB09, the remark
after Lemma 4.17]; proved): if `C` is `NL`-complete and
`C ∈ LOGSPACE`, then `NL = LOGSPACE`.

**Proof sketch.** `⊇` is `Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_NL` (phase P4.1). `⊆`:
a member of `NL` reduces to `C` (completeness) and
`Complexity.mem_LOGSPACE_of_logspaceReducible` pulls membership back along
the reduction. -/
theorem NL_eq_LOGSPACE_of_nlComplete_mem_LOGSPACE {C : Language Bool}
    (h : NLComplete C) (hC : C ∈ LOGSPACE) : NL = LOGSPACE := by
  exact Set.Subset.antisymm
    (fun B hB => mem_LOGSPACE_of_logspaceReducible (h.2 B hB) hC) LOGSPACE_subset_NL

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Machines/ARM.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.ParseCmp

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Abstract register machines

Logspace algorithms are usually described with a constant number of counters of logarithmic
size [AB09, §4.1]. An *abstract register machine* (`Complexity.LogProg.ARM`) is a flowchart
over finitely many labels whose registers hold natural numbers, with the instructions:
increment, decrement, clear, halve, zero/parity/equality tests, the input-format checks and
index comparisons of `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Parse`, subroutine calls,
and `ret b` (answer `b`). Its semantics (`Complexity.LogProg.astep`) is over values; the
compilation `Complexity.LogProg.armProg` into a register-tape program stores each register
in binary (`Nat.bits`) and implements each instruction by the fragment proved for it.

Related model: `Complexity.CounterProg` (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CounterProg`) is a
goto program over unary counters for the polynomial-time emitters of [AB09, §6.2]. It overlaps
in spirit with the programs here, which store registers in binary (as logarithmic space
requires) and call deciders on virtual inputs; the two are kept separate, and a polynomially
running counter program is simulated by an abstract register machine in
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.CounterProgSim`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.Ins`, `Complexity.LogProg.ARM` — instructions and machines.
* `Complexity.LogProg.astep` — the value semantics.
* `Complexity.LogProg.armProg` — the compiled register-tape program.
* `Complexity.LogProg.aseam` — the program configuration of an abstract configuration.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.astep_inc`, …, `Complexity.LogProg.astep_jeqSnd` — one step at each
  instruction.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

/-- The instructions of an abstract register machine over `m` registers calling `d` deciders,
with labels `Λ`. -/
inductive Ins (m d : ℕ) (Λ : Type) where
  /-- `r := r + 1` -/
  | inc (r : Fin m) (l : Λ)
  /-- `r := r - 1` (truncated) -/
  | dec (r : Fin m) (l : Λ)
  /-- `r := 0` -/
  | clr (r : Fin m) (l : Λ)
  /-- `r := r / 2` -/
  | half (r : Fin m) (l : Λ)
  /-- branch on `r = 0` -/
  | jz (r : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
  /-- branch on `r` odd -/
  | jodd (r : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
  /-- branch on `r = s` (distinct registers) -/
  | jeq (r s : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
  /-- call decider `j` on the virtual input of `mode` and `args` -/
  | call (j : Fin d) (mode : Mode) (args : List (Fin m)) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
  /-- answer `b` and halt -/
  | ret (b : Bool)
  /-- check that the input is `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩` with `w` a canonical binary payload (a `Nat.bits`
  word — `pairEncode [] [false]` has the pair shape but is rejected); else answer `0`;
  `r` is any register -/
  | valP (r : Fin m) (l : Λ)
  /-- check that the input is `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩` with both inner payloads canonical binary
  words (else answer `0`) -/
  | valQ (r : Fin m) (l : Λ)
  /-- branch on `Nat.bits r = w` for the input `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩` -/
  | jeqIn (r : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
  /-- branch on `Nat.bits r = u` for the input `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩` -/
  | jeqFst (r : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
  /-- branch on `Nat.bits r = w` for the input `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩` -/
  | jeqSnd (r : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)

/-- An abstract register machine: an instruction at every label. -/
abbrev ARM (m d : ℕ) (Λ : Type) := Λ → Ins m d Λ

/-- The word `w` of an input `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩`. -/
def plainWord (x : List Bool) : List Bool := x.drop (tRun x + 2)

/-- The words `u`, `w` of an input `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩`. -/
def pairWords (x : List Bool) : List Bool × List Bool :=
  (pairDecode (x.drop (tRun x + 2))).getD ([], [])

/-- The word of the input `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩` is `w`. -/
lemma plainWord_pairEncode (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    plainWord (pairEncode (List.replicate n true) w) = w := by
  unfold plainWord
  rw [tRun_pairEncode]
  simp [pairEncode_eq_dbl, dbl_replicate, List.drop_append]

/-- The words of the input `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩` are `u` and `w`. -/
lemma pairWords_pairEncode (n : ℕ) (u w : List Bool) :
    pairWords (pairEncode (List.replicate n true) (pairEncode u w)) = (u, w) := by
  have : (pairEncode (List.replicate n true) (pairEncode u w)).drop
      (tRun (pairEncode (List.replicate n true) (pairEncode u w)) + 2) = pairEncode u w := by
    rw [tRun_pairEncode]; simp [pairEncode_eq_dbl, dbl_replicate, List.drop_append]
  simp [pairWords, this, pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- An abstract configuration: the current label (`none` when halted), the register values,
and the answer once halted. -/
abbrev AConf (m : ℕ) (Λ : Type) := Option Λ × (Fin m → ℕ) × Option Bool

open Classical in
/-- **One step of an abstract register machine** on input `x`, deciders answering `oracle`. -/
noncomputable def astep {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool)
    (x : List Bool) : AConf m Λ → AConf m Λ
  | (none, v, res) => (none, v, res)
  | (some l, v, res) =>
    match A l with
    | .inc r l' => (some l', Function.update v r (v r + 1), res)
    | .dec r l' => (some l', Function.update v r (v r - 1), res)
    | .clr r l' => (some l', Function.update v r 0, res)
    | .half r l' => (some l', Function.update v r (v r / 2), res)
    | .jz r l₁ l₀ => (some (if v r = 0 then l₁ else l₀), v, res)
    | .jodd r l₁ l₀ => (some (if v r % 2 = 1 then l₁ else l₀), v, res)
    | .jeq r s l₁ l₀ => (some (if v r = v s then l₁ else l₀), v, res)
    | .call j md args l₁ l₀ =>
      (some (if oracle j (vword (callSegs ⟨j, md, args, l₁, l₀⟩ x (fun r => Nat.bits (v r))))
        then l₁ else l₀), v, res)
    | .ret b => (none, v, some b)
    | .valP _ l' => if ValidPlain x then (some l', v, res) else (none, v, some false)
    | .valQ _ l' => if ValidPair x then (some l', v, res) else (none, v, some false)
    | .jeqIn r l₁ l₀ => (some (if Nat.bits (v r) = plainWord x then l₁ else l₀), v, res)
    | .jeqFst r l₁ l₀ => (some (if Nat.bits (v r) = (pairWords x).1 then l₁ else l₀), v, res)
    | .jeqSnd r l₁ l₀ => (some (if Nat.bits (v r) = (pairWords x).2 then l₁ else l₀), v, res)

/-- The run of an abstract register machine. -/
noncomputable def arun {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool)
    (x : List Bool) (a : AConf m Λ) (n : ℕ) : AConf m Λ :=
  (astep A oracle x)^[n] a

/-- Running no steps stays put. -/
lemma arun_zero {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool)
    (x : List Bool) (a : AConf m Λ) : arun A oracle x a 0 = a := rfl

/-! ## One step, instruction by instruction

The value semantics of each instruction, stated as an equation for a live configuration
whose label holds it. -/

section Steps

variable {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} {A : ARM m d Λ} {oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool}
  {x : List Bool} {l : Λ} {v : Fin m → ℕ} {res : Option Bool}

/-- A step at an increment. -/
lemma astep_inc {r : Fin m} {l' : Λ} (h : A l = .inc r l') :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (some l', Function.update v r (v r + 1), res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a decrement. -/
lemma astep_dec {r : Fin m} {l' : Λ} (h : A l = .dec r l') :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (some l', Function.update v r (v r - 1), res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a clear. -/
lemma astep_clr {r : Fin m} {l' : Λ} (h : A l = .clr r l') :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (some l', Function.update v r 0, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a halving. -/
lemma astep_half {r : Fin m} {l' : Λ} (h : A l = .half r l') :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (some l', Function.update v r (v r / 2), res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a zero test. -/
lemma astep_jz {r : Fin m} {l₁ l₀ : Λ} (h : A l = .jz r l₁ l₀) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (some (if v r = 0 then l₁ else l₀), v, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a parity test. -/
lemma astep_jodd {r : Fin m} {l₁ l₀ : Λ} (h : A l = .jodd r l₁ l₀) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (some (if v r % 2 = 1 then l₁ else l₀), v, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at an equality test. -/
lemma astep_jeq {r s : Fin m} {l₁ l₀ : Λ} (h : A l = .jeq r s l₁ l₀) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (some (if v r = v s then l₁ else l₀), v, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a call: the decider's answer on the call's virtual input picks the branch. -/
lemma astep_call {j : Fin d} {md : Mode} {args : List (Fin m)} {l₁ l₀ : Λ}
    (h : A l = .call j md args l₁ l₀) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) =
      (some (if oracle j (vword (callSegs ⟨j, md, args, l₁, l₀⟩ x fun r => Nat.bits (v r)))
        then l₁ else l₀), v, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at an answer halts with it. -/
lemma astep_ret {b : Bool} (h : A l = .ret b) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) = (none, v, some b) := by
  simp [astep, h]

open Classical in
/-- A step at the plain-input check. -/
lemma astep_valP {r : Fin m} {l' : Λ} (h : A l = .valP r l') :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) =
      if ValidPlain x then (some l', v, res) else (none, v, some false) := by
  simp [astep, h]

open Classical in
/-- A step at the pair-input check. -/
lemma astep_valQ {r : Fin m} {l' : Λ} (h : A l = .valQ r l') :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) =
      if ValidPair x then (some l', v, res) else (none, v, some false) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a comparison with the word of a plain input. -/
lemma astep_jeqIn {r : Fin m} {l₁ l₀ : Λ} (h : A l = .jeqIn r l₁ l₀) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) =
      (some (if Nat.bits (v r) = plainWord x then l₁ else l₀), v, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a comparison with the first word of a pair input. -/
lemma astep_jeqFst {r : Fin m} {l₁ l₀ : Λ} (h : A l = .jeqFst r l₁ l₀) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) =
      (some (if Nat.bits (v r) = (pairWords x).1 then l₁ else l₀), v, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

/-- A step at a comparison with the second word of a pair input. -/
lemma astep_jeqSnd {r : Fin m} {l₁ l₀ : Λ} (h : A l = .jeqSnd r l₁ l₀) :
    astep A oracle x (some l, v, res) =
      (some (if Nat.bits (v r) = (pairWords x).2 then l₁ else l₀), v, res) := by
  simp [astep, h]

end Steps

/-! ## Compilation -/

/-- The phases of the instruction fragments. -/
inductive Ph where
  | start
  | incB
  | decL | decE | decB
  | clrE
  | h0 | hF | hT
  | eqBy | eqBn
  | vU1 | vS | vW0 | vWF | vWT | vrw1 | vrw2
  | vP1 (l : Option Bool) | vP2 (b : Bool) (l : Option Bool)
  | jK2 | jC | jRB (b : Bool) | jI1 (b : Bool) | jI2 (b : Bool)
  | jP1 | jP2F | jP2T | jD1 | jD2F | jD2T
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A control action: change state, move nothing. -/
def goAct {m : ℕ} {S : Type} (s : S) : Action m Bool S := ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some s⟩

/-- Halt with output `b`. -/
def retAct {m : ℕ} {S : Type} (b : Bool) : Action m Bool S := ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), some b, none⟩

/-- The input rewind scan (moving nothing else): left over symbols, then right into `nx`. -/
def rw2Act {m : ℕ} {S : Type} (r : Fin m) (s₀ nx : S) (a : Option Bool) : Action m Bool S :=
  match a with
  | some _ => xAct r (-1) 0 s₀
  | none => xAct r 1 0 nx

/-- The halting junk action. -/
def junkAct {m : ℕ} {S : Type} : Action m Bool S := ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩

/-- **The transition table of one instruction's fragment**: phase `start` is the fragment's
first state. -/
def insTr {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (i : Ins m d Λ) (l : Λ) (ph : Ph) (a : Option Bool)
    (w : Fin m → Option Bool) : Action m Bool (Λ × Ph) :=
  match i with
  | .inc r l' =>
    match ph with
    | .start => incCAct r (l, .start) (l, .incB) (w r)
    | .incB => incBAct r (l, .incB) (l', .start) (w r)
    | _ => junkAct
  | .dec r l' =>
    match ph with
    | .start => decDAct r (l, .start) (l, .decL) (l, .decB) (w r)
    | .decL => decLAct r (l, .decE) (l, .decB) (w r)
    | .decE => decEAct r (l, .decB)
    | .decB => incBAct r (l, .decB) (l', .start) (w r)
    | _ => junkAct
  | .clr r l' =>
    match ph with
    | .start => toEndAct r (l, .start) (l, .clrE) (w r)
    | .clrE => clrEAct r (l, .clrE) (l', .start) (w r)
    | _ => junkAct
  | .half r l' =>
    match ph with
    | .start => toEndAct r (l, .start) (l, .h0) (w r)
    | .h0 => halfLAct r none (l, .hF) (l, .hT) (l', .start) (w r)
    | .hF => halfLAct r (some false) (l, .hF) (l, .hT) (l', .start) (w r)
    | .hT => halfLAct r (some true) (l, .hF) (l, .hT) (l', .start) (w r)
    | _ => junkAct
  | .jz r l₁ l₀ =>
    match ph with
    | .start => goAct (if w r = none then (l₁, .start) else (l₀, .start))
    | _ => junkAct
  | .jodd r l₁ l₀ =>
    match ph with
    | .start => goAct (if w r = some true then (l₁, .start) else (l₀, .start))
    | _ => junkAct
  | .jeq r s l₁ l₀ =>
    match ph with
    | .start => eqCAct r s (l, .start) (l, .eqBy) (l, .eqBn) (w r) (w s)
    | .eqBy => eqBAct r s (l, .eqBy) (l₁, .start) (w r)
    | .eqBn => eqBAct r s (l, .eqBn) (l₀, .start) (w r)
    | _ => junkAct
  | .call _ _ _ _ _ => junkAct
  | .ret b =>
    match ph with
    | .start => retAct b
    | _ => junkAct
  | .valP r l' =>
    match ph with
    | .start => valUAct r (l, .start) (l, .vU1) (l, .vS) false a
    | .vU1 => valUAct r (l, .start) (l, .vU1) (l, .vS) true a
    | .vS => valSAct r (l, .vW0) a
    | .vW0 => valWAct r (l, .vWF) (l, .vWT) (l, .vrw1) none a
    | .vWF => valWAct r (l, .vWF) (l, .vWT) (l, .vrw1) (some false) a
    | .vWT => valWAct r (l, .vWF) (l, .vWT) (l, .vrw1) (some true) a
    | .vrw1 => xAct r (-1) 0 (l, .vrw2)
    | .vrw2 => rw2Act r (l, .vrw2) (l', .start) a
    | _ => junkAct
  | .valQ r l' =>
    match ph with
    | .start => valUAct r (l, .start) (l, .vU1) (l, .vS) false a
    | .vU1 => valUAct r (l, .start) (l, .vU1) (l, .vS) true a
    | .vS => valSAct r (l, .vP1 none) a
    | .vP1 lst => valP1Act r (fun b => (l, .vP2 b lst)) a
    | .vP2 b lst => valP2Act r (l, .vP1 (some false)) (l, .vP1 (some true)) (l, .vW0) lst b a
    | .vW0 => valWAct r (l, .vWF) (l, .vWT) (l, .vrw1) none a
    | .vWF => valWAct r (l, .vWF) (l, .vWT) (l, .vrw1) (some false) a
    | .vWT => valWAct r (l, .vWF) (l, .vWT) (l, .vrw1) (some true) a
    | .vrw1 => xAct r (-1) 0 (l, .vrw2)
    | .vrw2 => rw2Act r (l, .vrw2) (l', .start) a
    | _ => junkAct
  | .jeqIn r l₁ l₀ =>
    match ph with
    | .start => skipAct r (l, .start) (l, .jK2) a
    | .jK2 => xAct r 1 0 (l, .jC)
    | .jC => cmpAct r (l, .jC) (fun b => (l, .jRB b)) a (w r)
    | .jRB b => backAct r (l, .jRB b) (l, .jI1 b) (w r)
    | .jI1 b => xAct r (-1) 0 (l, .jI2 b)
    | .jI2 b => rewAct r (l, .jI2 b) (if b then (l₁, .start) else (l₀, .start)) a
    | _ => junkAct
  | .jeqSnd r l₁ l₀ =>
    match ph with
    | .start => skipAct r (l, .start) (l, .jK2) a
    | .jK2 => xAct r 1 0 (l, .jP1)
    | .jP1 => pskip1Act r (l, .jP2F) (l, .jP2T) a
    | .jP2F => pskip2Act r (l, .jP1) (l, .jC) false a
    | .jP2T => pskip2Act r (l, .jP1) (l, .jC) true a
    | .jC => cmpAct r (l, .jC) (fun b => (l, .jRB b)) a (w r)
    | .jRB b => backAct r (l, .jRB b) (l, .jI1 b) (w r)
    | .jI1 b => xAct r (-1) 0 (l, .jI2 b)
    | .jI2 b => rewAct r (l, .jI2 b) (if b then (l₁, .start) else (l₀, .start)) a
    | _ => junkAct
  | .jeqFst r l₁ l₀ =>
    match ph with
    | .start => skipAct r (l, .start) (l, .jK2) a
    | .jK2 => xAct r 1 0 (l, .jD1)
    | .jD1 => dcmp1Act r (l, .jD2F) (l, .jD2T) a
    | .jD2F => dcmp2Act r (l, .jD1) (fun b => (l, .jRB b)) false a (w r)
    | .jD2T => dcmp2Act r (l, .jD1) (fun b => (l, .jRB b)) true a (w r)
    | .jRB b => backAct r (l, .jRB b) (l, .jI1 b) (w r)
    | .jI1 b => xAct r (-1) 0 (l, .jI2 b)
    | .jI2 b => rewAct r (l, .jI2 b) (if b then (l₁, .start) else (l₀, .start)) a
    | _ => junkAct

/-- The transition table of the compiled program. -/
def armTr {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ) (l : Λ) (ph : Ph) (a : Option Bool)
    (w : Fin m → Option Bool) : Action m Bool (Λ × Ph) :=
  insTr (A l) l ph a w

/-- The call node of one instruction. -/
def insCall {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (i : Ins m d Λ) (ph : Ph) : Option (CallSpec m d (Λ × Ph)) :=
  match i with
  | .call j md args l₁ l₀ =>
    match ph with
    | .start => some ⟨j, md, args, (l₁, .start), (l₀, .start)⟩
    | _ => none
  | _ => none

/-- The call nodes of the compiled program. -/
def armCall {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ) (q : Λ × Ph) :
    Option (CallSpec m d (Λ × Ph)) :=
  insCall (A q.1) q.2

/-- **The compiled register-tape program** of an abstract register machine. -/
def armProg {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) : RProg m d (Λ × Ph) where
  tm := ⟨(l₀, .start), fun q a w => armTr A q.1 q.2 a w⟩
  call := armCall A

/-- The program configuration representing the abstract configuration at label `l` with
values `v`, having written `out`. -/
def aseam {m : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (x : List Bool) (l : Λ) (v : Fin m → ℕ) (out : List Bool) :
    Cfg m Bool (Λ × Ph) x :=
  ⟨some (l, .start), ⟨1, by omega⟩, fun r => FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits (v r)), fun _ => 0, out⟩

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMProof
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ImplicitPoly

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# A toolkit for abstract register machines

Conveniences for writing logspace algorithms as abstract register machines
(`Complexity.LogProg.ARM`) on inputs `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩`: the virtual inputs of calls in `unaryFst`
mode with one or two register arguments are `⟨1ⁿ, bits r⟩` and `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨bits r, bits s⟩⟩`,
and `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_poly` restates `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides` with
register values bounded by a polynomial in the input length.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.vword_unary₁`, `Complexity.LogProg.vword_unary₂` — virtual inputs
  of `unaryFst` calls.
* `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_poly` — abstract register machines with polynomially
  bounded register values decide languages in `L`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

variable {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type}

/-- The leading run of `1`s of `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩` is `1²ⁿ`. -/
lemma takeWhile_pairEncode_replicate (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    (pairEncode (List.replicate n true) w).takeWhile (· = true) =
      List.replicate (2 * n) true := by
  simp only [pairEncode_eq_dbl, dbl_replicate, List.append_assoc]
  rw [List.takeWhile_append_of_pos (by simp)]
  simp

/-- The virtual input of a `unaryFst` call with one argument on `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩` is `⟨1ⁿ, V r⟩`. -/
lemma vword_unary₁ (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (j : Fin d) (r : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
    (V : Fin m → List Bool) :
    vword (callSegs ⟨j, .unaryFst, [r], l₁, l₀⟩ (pairEncode (List.replicate n true) w) V) =
      pairEncode (List.replicate n true) (V r) := by
  simp only [callSegs, Mode.seg0, takeWhile_pairEncode_replicate, List.map_cons,
    List.map_nil, argSegs, vword, render, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
  simp [pairEncode_eq_dbl, dbl_replicate]

/-- The virtual input of a `unaryFst` call with two arguments on `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩` is
`⟨1ⁿ, ⟨V r, V s⟩⟩`. -/
lemma vword_unary₂ (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) (j : Fin d) (r s : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
    (V : Fin m → List Bool) :
    vword (callSegs ⟨j, .unaryFst, [r, s], l₁, l₀⟩ (pairEncode (List.replicate n true) w) V) =
      pairEncode (List.replicate n true) (pairEncode (V r) (V s)) := by
  simp only [callSegs, Mode.seg0, takeWhile_pairEncode_replicate, List.map_cons,
    List.map_nil, argSegs, vword, render, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
  simp [pairEncode_eq_dbl, dbl_replicate]

/-- The indicator of a set at a point, as a decision. -/
lemma indicator_eq_decide {α : Type} (S : Set α) (a : α) :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator S a = @decide (a ∈ S) (Classical.dec _) := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.indicator; split <;> simp_all

/-- **Abstract register machines with polynomially bounded registers decide languages in
`L`**: the form of `arm_decides` with register values at most `C₀ (|x| + 1)^{c₀}`.

**Proof sketch.** A value `v ≤ C₀ (|x|+1)^{c₀}` has `|bits (v + 1)| ≤ ⌊log₂ (v + 1)⌋ + 1`,
which `log_poly_bound` bounds by `K · logSpace |x|`. -/
theorem arm_decides_poly {L : Language Bool} [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ] (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (l₀ : Λ) (As : Fin d → Language Bool) (hAs : ∀ j, As j ∈ LOGSPACE) (C₀ c₀ : ℕ)
    (hcorr : ∀ x, AHalt A (fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (As j : Set (List Bool)) V) x
      (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ C₀ * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀)
      (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) (MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x)) :
    L ∈ LOGSPACE := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := log_poly_bound C₀ c₀ 1
  refine arm_decides A l₀ As hAs K fun x => (hcorr x).mono fun a ⟨h1, h2⟩ => ⟨h1, fun r => ?_⟩
  have e1 := length_bits_le_log (a.2.1 r + 1)
  have e2 : Nat.log 2 (a.2.1 r + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 (C₀ * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀ + 1) :=
    Nat.log_mono_right (by have := h2 r; omega)
  have e3 := hK x.length
  simp only [logSpace]
  omega

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.InputAccess

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Bounded runs and counting loops of abstract register machines

The guard `Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe A x B` of bounded runs of an abstract register machine
(`Complexity.LogProg.ARM`): a configuration meets it when it satisfies the syntactic
preconditions `Complexity.LogProg.PreS` and all its registers are at most `B`. It is
definitionally the guard of the shared fragments of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.InputAccess` (`registerCopy_loop`, …), so their
runs compose with runs through `GuardLe`. It is used by the codec checkers
(`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Engine`) and the Savitch machine
(`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM`).

The file also proves run lemmas for the counting loops out of which register-machine
arithmetic is built: moving a register into one or two others (`move_run`, `move2_run`),
moving it doubled (`dmove_run`), subtracting (`sub_run`), halving a register as often as a
counter says (`halve_run`), copying through a scratch register (`copy_run`) and shifting left
by a counter (`shl_run`). Each lemma is stated for an arbitrary abstract register machine
whose instructions at the loop's labels have the loop's shape, as a run through `GuardLe`.

Infrastructure for the register-machine description of space-bounded algorithms of
[AB09, §4.1]; not itself a result of the book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe` — the guard: syntactic preconditions and registers at most
  `B`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe.of_preS` — introducing the guard.
* `Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.embed_guardLe` — a bounded halting run of a block, inside a
  larger machine.
* `Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq` — rewriting the end configuration of a run.
* `Complexity.LogProg.move_run`, `move2_run`, `dmove_run`, `sub_run`, `halve_run` — the
  single loops.
* `Complexity.LogProg.copy_run`, `shl_run` — the composite loops.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

variable {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type}

/-- **The bounded-run guard**: the syntactic preconditions, and every register at most `B`. -/
abbrev GuardLe (A : ARM m d Λ) (x : List Bool) (B : ℕ) : AConf m Λ → Prop :=
  fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B

variable {A : ARM m d Λ} {oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {B : ℕ}

/-- A configuration meeting the syntactic preconditions with registers at most `B` meets the
guard. -/
lemma GuardLe.of_preS {a : AConf m Λ} (h : PreS A x a) (hv : ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) :
    GuardLe A x B a := ⟨h, hv⟩

/-- **A bounded halting run of a block, inside a larger machine**: if `A`, its deciders read
through `σ`, answers `b` from `l` with registers at most `B`, then a larger machine holding
`A`'s table as a block (`Complexity.LogProg.Ins.embed`) runs from the image of `l` to the exit
`k b` with registers at most `B' ≥ B`, provided its own registers (`e`, off `ρ`'s range) are at
most `B'`. It ends with the block's registers at most `B` and its own registers unchanged.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.embed`; the guard carries over because the
syntactic preconditions do (`Complexity.LogProg.preS_embed`) and every register of the larger
machine is either an image of one of `A`'s or one of its own. -/
theorem AHalt.embed_guardLe {m' d' : ℕ} {Λ' : Type} {D : ARM m' d' Λ'} {ρ : Fin m → Fin m'}
    {σ : Fin d → Fin d'} {ι : Λ → Λ'} {k : Bool → Λ'} {r₀ : Fin m'}
    (hρ : Function.Injective ρ) (hD : ∀ l, D (ι l) = (A l).embed ρ σ ι k r₀)
    (hA : ∀ l r l', A l ≠ .valP r l' ∧ A l ≠ .valQ r l') {oracle' : Fin d' → List Bool → Bool}
    {B' : ℕ} (hBB : B ≤ B') {e : Fin m' → ℕ} (he : ∀ r', e r' ≤ B') {l : Λ} {v : Fin m → ℕ}
    {b : Bool} (h : AHalt A (oracle' ∘ σ) x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none) b)
    {v' : Fin m' → ℕ} (hv : RegExt ρ e v v') :
    ∃ v₂', (∀ r', (∀ r, ρ r ≠ r') → v₂' r' = e r') ∧ (∀ r, v₂' (ρ r) ≤ B) ∧
      AReach D oracle' x (GuardLe D x B') (some (ι l), v', none) (some (k b), v₂', none) := by
  have hG : ∀ l v v', GuardLe A x B (some l, v, none) → RegExt ρ e v v' →
      GuardLe D x B' (some (ι l), v', none) := by
    intro l v v' hg hv
    refine ⟨preS_embed hρ hD hg.1, fun r' => ?_⟩
    show v' r' ≤ B'
    by_cases hr : ∃ r, ρ r = r'
    · obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hr
      rw [hv.reg]
      exact (hg.2 r).trans hBB
    · push_neg at hr
      rw [hv.ext r' hr]
      exact he r'
  obtain ⟨v₂, v₂', ⟨l₂, hg₂⟩, hv₂, hr⟩ := AHalt.embed hρ hD hA hG h hv
  exact ⟨v₂', hv₂.ext, fun r => (hv₂.reg r).symm ▸ hg₂.2 r, hr⟩

/-- A run whose end configuration is rewritten along an equation. -/
lemma reach_of_eq {G : AConf m Λ → Prop} {a b b' : AConf m Λ} (h : AReach A oracle x G a b)
    (e : b = b') : AReach A oracle x G a b' := e ▸ h

/-! ## Counting loops -/

/-- **Moving a register into another**: the loop `l: jz r lx l₁; l₁: dec r l₂; l₂: inc t l`
adds `r` to `t` and clears `r`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `r`: each round moves one unit. -/
theorem move_run {l lx l1 l2 : Λ} {r t : Fin m} (hrt : r ≠ t)
    (h0 : A l = .jz r lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec r l2) (h2 : A l2 = .inc t l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v r = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v t + v r ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r) = v := by
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = t
      · subst hs; simp [hk]
      · by_cases hs' : s = r
        · subst hs'; simp [hs, hk]
        · simp [hs, hs']
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv hb
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_dec h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], fun s => ?_⟩ ?_
    · by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs; simp; omega
      · simp [hs]; exact hv s
    simp only [astep_inc h2, Function.update_of_ne (Ne.symm hrt)]
    have hb2 : ∀ s, Function.update (Function.update v r k) t (v t + 1) s ≤ B := by
      intro s
      by_cases hs : s = t
      · subst hs; simp; omega
      · by_cases hs' : s = r
        · subst hs'; simp [hs]; omega
        · simp [hs, hs']; exact hv s
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hrt]) hb2 (by simp [hrt]; omega)) ?_
    · congr 2
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = t
      · subst hs; simp [hrt]; omega
      · by_cases hs' : s = r
        · subst hs'; simp [hs]
        · simp [hs, hs']

/-- Close a goal about updated register files by cases on the register. -/
local macro "upd_tac" : tactic =>
  `(tactic| (funext s; simp only [Function.update_apply]; split_ifs <;> subst_vars <;>
    (try simp_all) <;> omega))

/-- **Moving a register into two others**: the loop
`l: jz r lx l₁; l₁: dec r l₂; l₂: inc t l₃; l₃: inc t' l` adds `r` to `t` and to `t'` and
clears `r`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `r`: each round moves one unit into both. -/
theorem move2_run {l lx l1 l2 l3 : Λ} {r t t' : Fin m} (hrt : r ≠ t) (hrt' : r ≠ t')
    (htt : t ≠ t')
    (h0 : A l = .jz r lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec r l2) (h2 : A l2 = .inc t l3)
    (h3 : A l3 = .inc t' l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v r = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v t + v r ≤ B → v t' + v r ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r)) t'
        (v t' + v r), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv _ _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r)) t'
        (v t' + v r) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv hb hb'
    have hr := hv r
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_dec h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have b1 := register_update_le _ r _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], b1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_inc h2]
    have b2 := register_update_le _ t _ _ b1 (show Function.update v r k t + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt]; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h3], b2⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_inc h3]
    have b3 := register_update_le _ t' _ _ b2 (show Function.update (Function.update v r k) t
        (Function.update v r k t + 1) t' + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt', Ne.symm htt]; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hrt, hrt']) b3
      (by simp [hrt, hrt', htt, Ne.symm htt, Ne.symm hrt, Ne.symm hrt']; omega)
      (by simp [hrt, hrt', Ne.symm htt, Ne.symm hrt, Ne.symm hrt']; omega)) ?_
    congr 2
    upd_tac

/-- **Moving a register doubled**: the loop
`l: jz r lx l₁; l₁: dec r l₂; l₂: inc t l₃; l₃: inc t l` adds `2r` to `t` and clears `r`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `r`: each round moves one unit twice. -/
theorem dmove_run {l lx l1 l2 l3 : Λ} {r t : Fin m} (hrt : r ≠ t)
    (h0 : A l = .jz r lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec r l2) (h2 : A l2 = .inc t l3)
    (h3 : A l3 = .inc t l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v r = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v t + 2 * v r ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + 2 * v r), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + 2 * v r) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv hb
    have hr := hv r
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_dec h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have b1 := register_update_le _ r _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], b1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_inc h2]
    have b2 := register_update_le _ t _ _ b1 (show Function.update v r k t + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt]; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h3], b2⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_inc h3]
    have b3 := register_update_le _ t _ _ b2 (show Function.update (Function.update v r k) t
        (Function.update v r k t + 1) t + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt]; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hrt]) b3 (by simp [hrt, Ne.symm hrt]; omega)) ?_
    congr 2
    upd_tac

/-- **Subtracting a register**: the loop `l: jz q lx l₁; l₁: dec q l₂; l₂: dec r l`
subtracts `q` from `r` (truncated) and clears `q`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `q`: each round removes one unit. -/
theorem sub_run {l lx l1 l2 : Λ} {q r : Fin m} (hqr : q ≠ r)
    (h0 : A l = .jz q lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec q l2) (h2 : A l2 = .dec r l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v q = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v q 0) r (v r - v q), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v q 0) r (v r - v q) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_dec h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have b1 := register_update_le _ q _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by have := hv q; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], b1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_dec h2]
    have b2 := register_update_le _ r _ _ b1 (show Function.update v q k r - 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hqr]; have := hv r; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hqr]) b2) ?_
    congr 2
    upd_tac

/-- **Halving a register as often as a counter says**: the loop
`l: jz c lx l₁; l₁: dec c l₂; l₂: half r l` divides `r` by `2 ^ c` and clears `c`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `c`: `⌊⌊r / 2⌋ / 2 ^ k⌋ = ⌊r / 2 ^ (k + 1)⌋`. -/
theorem halve_run {l lx l1 l2 : Λ} {c r : Fin m} (hcr : c ≠ r)
    (h0 : A l = .jz c lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec c l2) (h2 : A l2 = .half r l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v c = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r / 2 ^ v c), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r / 2 ^ v c) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_jz h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_dec h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have hb1 : ∀ s, Function.update v c k s ≤ B :=
      register_update_le _ _ _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by have := hv c; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], hb1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_half h2]
    have hb2 : ∀ s, Function.update (Function.update v c k) r (Function.update v c k r / 2) s
        ≤ B := by
      intro s
      by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs; simp [Ne.symm hcr]; exact (Nat.div_le_self _ _).trans (hv _)
      · simp only [Function.update_of_ne hs]; exact hb1 s
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hcr]) hb2) ?_
    congr 2
    funext s
    by_cases hs : s = r
    · subst hs
      simp [hcr, Ne.symm hcr, Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul, pow_succ, mul_comm]
    · by_cases hs' : s = c
      · subst hs'; simp [hs]
      · simp [hs, hs']

/-- **Copying a register through a scratch register**: the loops
`l: jz src l₄ l₁; l₁: dec src l₂; l₂: inc dst l₃; l₃: inc z l` and
`l₄: jz z lx l₅; l₅: dec z l₆; l₆: inc src l₄`, with `z` clear, add `src` to `dst` and leave
everything else unchanged.

**Proof sketch.** `move2_run` moves `src` into `dst` and `z`, `move_run` moves `z` back. -/
theorem copy_run {l l1 l2 l3 l4 l5 l6 lx : Λ} {src dst z : Fin m} (h1 : src ≠ dst)
    (h2 : src ≠ z) (h3 : dst ≠ z)
    (a0 : A l = .jz src l4 l1) (a1 : A l1 = .dec src l2) (a2 : A l2 = .inc dst l3)
    (a3 : A l3 = .inc z l) (a4 : A l4 = .jz z lx l5) (a5 : A l5 = .dec z l6)
    (a6 : A l6 = .inc src l4)
    (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hz : v z = 0) (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B) (hb : v dst + v src ≤ B) :
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update v dst (v dst + v src), none) := by
  refine (move2_run h1 h2 h3 a0 a1 a2 a3 _ v rfl hv hb (by have := hv src; omega)).trans ?_
  have b1 := register_update_le _ z _ _
    (register_update_le _ dst _ _ (register_update_le _ src _ _ hv (Nat.zero_le B)) hb)
    (show v z + v src ≤ B by have := hv src; omega)
  refine reach_of_eq (move_run (Ne.symm h2) a4 a5 a6 _ _ rfl b1
    (by simp [h1, h2, hz]; exact hv src)) ?_
  congr 2
  upd_tac

/-- **Shifting a register left as often as a counter says**: the loops
`l: jz c lx l₁; l₁: dec c l₂`, then `l₂ … l₅` moving `r` doubled into `z` (exit `l₆`), then
`l₆ … l₈` moving `z` back into `r` (exit `l`), with `z` clear, multiply `r` by `2 ^ c` and
clear `c`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `c`: each round doubles `r` (`dmove_run`,
`move_run`). -/
theorem shl_run {l l1 l2 l3 l4 l5 l6 l7 l8 lx : Λ} {c r z : Fin m} (hcr : c ≠ r) (hcz : c ≠ z)
    (hrz : r ≠ z)
    (a0 : A l = .jz c lx l1) (a1 : A l1 = .dec c l2) (a2 : A l2 = .jz r l6 l3)
    (a3 : A l3 = .dec r l4) (a4 : A l4 = .inc z l5) (a5 : A l5 = .inc z l2)
    (a6 : A l6 = .jz z l l7) (a7 : A l7 = .dec z l8) (a8 : A l8 = .inc r l6) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v c = k → v z = 0 → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v r * 2 ^ v c ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r * 2 ^ v c), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk _ hv _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, a0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r * 2 ^ v c) = v := by
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs; simp [hk]
      · by_cases hs' : s = c
        · subst hs'; simp [hs, hk]
        · simp [hs, hs']
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep_jz a0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hz hv hb
    have h2 : 2 * v r ≤ B := by
      rw [hk, pow_succ] at hb
      have : 2 ≤ 2 ^ k * 2 := by have := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := k); omega
      calc 2 * v r ≤ v r * (2 ^ k * 2) := by rw [mul_comm]; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ this
        _ ≤ B := hb
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, a0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_jz a0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, a1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep_dec a1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have hv1 : ∀ s, Function.update v c k s ≤ B :=
      register_update_le _ _ _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by have := hv c; omega)
    refine (dmove_run hrz a2 a3 a4 a5 _ _ rfl hv1
      (by simp [Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)).trans ?_
    have hv2 := register_update_le _ z _ _ (register_update_le _ r _ _ hv1 (Nat.zero_le B))
      (show Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r ≤ B by
        simp [Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)
    refine (move_run (Ne.symm hrz) a6 a7 a8 _ _ rfl hv2
      (by simp [hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)).trans ?_
    have hv3 : ∀ s, Function.update (Function.update (Function.update (Function.update
        (Function.update v c k) r 0) z (Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r))
        z 0) r (Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v c k) r 0) z
        (Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r) r +
        Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v c k) r 0) z
        (Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r) z) s ≤ B :=
      register_update_le _ _ _ _ (register_update_le _ _ _ _ hv2 (Nat.zero_le B)) (by
        simp [hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hcr, hcz]) (by simp [hrz, Ne.symm hrz]) hv3 ?_) ?_
    · simp [hcr, hcz, hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]
      rw [hk, pow_succ] at hb
      calc 2 * v r * 2 ^ k = v r * (2 ^ k * 2) := by ring
        _ ≤ B := hb
    · congr 2
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs
        simp [hcr, hcz, hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz, pow_succ]; ring
      · by_cases hs' : s = c
        · subst hs'; simp [hs, hcz]
        · by_cases hs'' : s = z
          · subst hs''; simp [hs, hs', hz]
          · simp [hs, hs', hs'']

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-
